intro: The people I learn from, most of them from a distance through their videos and books. Each one gives me something specific, and each one shows up on the channel in a specific way.

mentors.name: Linus Tech Tips
mentors.who: Linus Sebastian's tech channel, which grew into a whole media company with a team behind it.
learn: Make tech entertaining without dumbing it down
Consistency, and a channel run like a company
Personality in front of the hardware
mentors.channel: Bring personality to tool videos, and treat the channel as a system with a weekly rhythm, not one-off posts.

mentors.name: Ali Abdaal
mentors.who: A doctor turned YouTuber and author, known for evidence-based productivity. He studied medicine at Cambridge.
learn: Evidence-based, calm explanations
Systems over willpower
Teaching what you're learning, in public
mentors.channel: Self-learning videos built on a system viewers can copy. There's also a shared Cambridge connection.

mentors.name: İlker Canıkligil
mentors.who: A Turkish film director and writer who taught directing at Istanbul Film Academy, then moved into making YouTube content.
learn: Storytelling and directing craft
Framing a scene so it means something
A Turkish voice making the move to YouTube
mentors.channel: Film craft for the formats (Pilot's Log, co-host sketches): shot choice, pacing and story structure.

mentors.name: Greg Edits Video
mentors.who: A YouTube channel about the craft of video editing.
learn: Editing as storytelling: what to cut, and when
Pacing that keeps people watching
Polish that makes a solo creator look like a studio
mentors.channel: Tighter edits on long videos (your junior-dev video's payoff sat at 8:35) and sharper Shorts: cut to the hook faster.

mentors.name: Patrick Bet-David
mentors.who: An Iranian-born immigrant to the US who became an entrepreneur and built Valuetainment and the PBD Podcast. Author of 'Your Next Five Moves'.
learn: Think several moves ahead, like chess
An immigrant's drive turned into a business
Content as a business engine
mentors.channel: Strategy thinking (fits your love of RTS games), and the B2C2B path from viewers to Skool to business services.

mentors.name: Tony Robbins
mentors.who: A life coach, author and speaker known for energy, belief and big live events.
learn: State and energy change outcomes
Belief comes before action
A clear, confident call to action
mentors.channel: End every video with optimism and a plan (like the 90-day flight plan), not hype.

mentors.name: David R. Hawkins
mentors.who: A psychiatrist and author ('Power vs. Force'), best known for his Map of Consciousness.
learn: A map for levels of consciousness
Moving from fear towards courage and peace
Inner work as part of the work
mentors.channel: The consciousness thread on 'What I care about'. Present it as a framework, not science, to stay honest about AI.

mentors.name: Eric Wroolie
mentors.todo: No public profile found, so this card is waiting for your words. Add who Eric is and what he taught you in data/mentors.json.

mentors.name: Barış Özcan
mentors.who: A Turkish storyteller on YouTube who explains science, technology and history through calm, curious stories.
learn: Curiosity as the hook: start with a question
Calm narration that makes complex topics feel simple
Story first, facts woven in
mentors.channel: Open Pillar 2 videos with a question and a story, and reach Turkish-speaking viewers with the same craft.

mentors.name: Kallaway
mentors.who: A creator who teaches short-form storytelling and content strategy: hooks, structure and retention.
learn: Hooks that earn the next 3 seconds
Story structure for short-form
Packaging: title, thumbnail and first line as one promise
mentors.channel: Sharper Shorts hooks, and fixing packaging gaps like the junior-dev video's title/description mismatch.

mentors.name: After Skool
mentors.who: An animated channel that turns big ideas from thinkers into hand-drawn, whiteboard-style stories with voiceover.
learn: Simple drawings make ideas memorable
One idea per video, illustrated as it's spoken
Voice plus visuals instead of a talking head
mentors.channel: Pairs with the single-line format (Formats page): illustrate one idea per video in your own original drawn style.

mentors.name: Alex Hormozi
mentors.who: An entrepreneur and investor known for '$100M Offers' and '$100M Leads', and for giving away business advice in volume.
learn: Make offers so good people feel stupid saying no
Give away the 'what' and the 'how', and sell the implementation
Volume and consistency win
mentors.channel: Design the 💼 Professional and 🏢 Business tiers as irresistible offers (see the Business plan).

mentors.name: Daniel Priestley
mentors.who: An entrepreneur and author ('Key Person of Influence', 'Oversubscribed') who teaches founders to become known in their niche.
learn: Become a key person of influence in one niche
Publish, build products, raise your profile
Create demand before supply (oversubscribed)
mentors.channel: Own the 'Delivery Pilot' niche: publish (the research paper), productise (the bots), profile (the channel).

mentors.name: Mark Manson
mentors.who: An author ('The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck') who writes about values, responsibility and an honest life.
learn: Choose what to care about
Take responsibility, even for what isn't your fault
Honest and blunt, but with heart
mentors.channel: Your directness (Agreeableness 0) with values underneath: honest takes on AI and work, never cynical.

takeaway: 🧑‍✈️ Put together: Linus's energy, Ali's systems, İlker's directing, Greg's editing, Barış and Kallaway's storytelling, After Skool's drawn style, Hormozi's offers, Priestley's influence, PBD's strategy, Manson's values, Tony's belief and Hawkins' inner map, all pointed at one mission: helping people become Delivery Pilots.
